intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Jackson County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: The results of our tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards.
verdicts.detail: On internal control, the auditors wrote: “During our audit we did not identify any deficiencies in internal control that we consider to be material weaknesses.”

verdicts.quote: The following deficiencies were noted during the review of the Circuit Clerk's office: • The Fee, Receipting, and Fidlar bank reconciliations were not always prepared in accordance with Ark. Code Ann. § 14-25-107. • The Receipting and Fidlar journals contained posting errors related to beginning cash balances, receipting, disbursements, and ending cash balances.
verdicts.detail: The auditors also reported these matters to county officials in a separate letter. The letter continues in the report on page 8; parts that concern staff positions are left to the report, since this site doesn’t single out non-elected staff.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated September 18, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.
